fixes: tariff.VERSION, the pyproject version and requires-python now follow package_manifest.json.
The requests dependency is gone: pyproject declares no dependency and the package imports the standard library only.
python -m tariff now accepts --statements, exits 2 and writes 'missing input: <file>' on standard error when an input file is missing.
The README no longer describes the 30-day proration and names the optional input files and the statement run.
The two visible tests that asserted the 30-day proration and a credit below the commitment now assert what the contract says.
A tier now covers the account positions up to and including its up_to; it used to stop one unit short of it.
Units are rated from the position they hold among the account's units over all its meters instead of restarting the tiers at every meter.
A standing line is now the sum, over the meter's active days, of the standing charge of the day divided by the days of that day's own month, in place of a flat 30-day month.
The standing charge of a day follows the plan's standing_changes entry with the latest from date on or before that day.
Every amount is computed from the decimal values as written in the input files with exact fractions and rounded half to even to 0.01, instead of binary floats.
Added the allowance sharing of the energy lines: equal parts capped at a line's exact value, re-shared while some stays unshared, and the remainder reported back.

The commitment credit is now measured on the invoice subtotal rather than on a second base that also rated refused reads, the total is the discounted subtotal rounded half to even and the credit is what the total takes off the subtotal.
Added the voucher redemption: the largest voucher sum not above the balance, taking the set whose id list comes first.
A quantity is a usable quantity only when it is a JSON integer of 0 or more, so text, decimals, booleans and null now receive malformed_quantity.
Added the missing outside_period exception for a read whose day lies in no billing period of its account.
Added the missing replaced_estimate exception for an estimate whose day already has an accepted measured read.
duplicate_read now compares the estimated flag as well and only fires against an earlier read that was itself accepted.
The exception list is sorted by read_id alone; it used to be sorted by account first.
Reads now carry their estimated and cumulative flags, and billed_quantities bills a cumulative read as the rise over the previous accepted cumulative read of its meter.
A meter can hold several active windows for one account, so inactive_meter looks at every row of accounts.csv for the pair.
Every row of billing_periods.csv is billed as its own invoice, sorted by account and then by start; the engine used to keep one invoice per account and silently drop the account's other rows.
A read is counted on the invoice whose period holds its day, and the period quantities, positions and active days of an invoice come from that row alone.
Active days are counted day by day inside the period over the meter's own windows, which also fixes periods that span two months.
The plan of a row is found by plan name or by one of the plan's codes.
Added the tier revision choice: a plan is rated with the one revision under which every paid invoice on the plan totals its paid amount.
The allowance that no energy line can take is carried to the account's next invoice by start and dropped after the last one.
An invoice gets no credit when the account's previous invoice by start was paid less than its total, which needed the optional payments.csv.
Added the statement document built from vouchers.csv: balance, redeemed voucher ids and what is due.
Every amount in the document is written as a string with exactly two decimals.
Added missing_input so the command line can name the first input file a directory lacks.
